svg.text: The final common path: from motor neuron to force
Every descending and reflex command is squeezed through the lower motor neuron. Muscle and tendon mechanics then decide what that command produces.
One motor unit, and the two motor outflows that reach a muscle
α motor neurons drive the force-producing extrafusal fibres; γ motor neurons set the sensitivity of the spindles inside them.
α and γ neurons of one pool sit in the ventral horn
intrafusal fibres, in parallel with the rest
One α motor neuron and every fibre it innervates is one motor unit
Its fibres are scattered among fibres of other units. γ drive keeps the spindle responsive as the muscle shortens.
schematic; real ratios span 10 to 1000+ fibres
Recruitment and rate coding on one shared axis
As drive rises, active units fire faster and new units join.
motor-pool drive, ramped slowly and linearly
smaller soma, fewer fibres, recruited earlier
larger soma, more fibres, recruited later
Dashed lines mark recruitment thresholds; the open circles show where each new unit
joins the force curve. Size ordering is a strong tendency rather than a fixed sequence,
and firing rate depends on neuromodulatory drive too, not on synaptic input alone.
The same output, three loads, three forces
Only the external load differs. Resting length and neural drive are identical in all three.
same units recruited, same firing rates
The three contractions differ only in load, so they differ only in velocity. Force follows the
force–velocity relation, not the drive. Eccentric force above F0 is clearest in isolated preparations
and smaller in voluntary contractions; length, tendon compliance and prior activation shift it further.
The lower motor neuron is the last point where the nervous system decides anything. Mechanics decides what that produces.
